definition: Taking part in a physical or angry struggle.
example: The two brothers were fighting over a toy car.
note: The example had a stray word at the end ('a toy car toy'). Cleaned up. The four languages were in different shapes; they now all use the same '-ing' form.

definition: Traditional, in the style of the ordinary people of a country.
example: The folk music tells stories of ancient times.
note: Spanish and German were describing words while French and Italian were the thing itself. All four now describe, matching 'folk music' in the example.

definition: More; additional.
example: I need further information about the project.
note: The example repeated itself ('about the project details of the new project development'). Cleaned up. Spanish just said 'more'; changed to 'additional' so all four match. Italian was plural; made singular.

definition: To watch over something to keep it safe.
example: The dog will guard the house all night long.
note: Italian 'proteggere' means 'to protect', which is a different idea. Changed to 'sorvegliare', the word for watching over something.

definition: Very eager and interested.
example: She is a keen student and loves to learn.
note: French 'désireux' means 'wanting something'. Changed to 'enthousiaste' so all four say the same thing.

definition: The most recent.
example: Have you seen the latest news about the election?
note: French and Italian said 'last' while Spanish and German said 'most recent'. All four now say 'most recent', matching the definition.

definition: Alive.
example: All plants and animals are living organisms.
note: German 'lebende' carried a grammar ending the other three did not have. Changed to the plain form 'lebend'.

definition: Certainly or unavoidably; most often used in the negative, 'not necessarily'.
example: He does not necessarily agree with the new rules.
note: The definition said 'in every case; always', but the example was a negative sentence, so the two did not agree. Definition rewritten to match how the word is really used.

definition: To have to have something because it is necessary.
example: I need water to drink and stay alive.
note: Same word appears twice in the list; corrected the same way so the two entries agree.

definition: Coming immediately after this one.
example: The next train arrives in five minutes.
note: Italian capital letter removed.

definition: Belonging to an earlier time; no longer in style.
example: She likes to wear old-fashioned clothes from the 1950s.
note: French 'désuet' is a bookish word meaning 'obsolete'. The everyday word for clothes that are out of style is 'démodé'.

definition: The act of deciding and arranging what to do.
example: Careful planning made the trip run smoothly.
note: The headword is the thing, and the definition describes the thing, but all four translations had been turned into the action. Restored to the thing, and the example now shows it as a thing.

definition: A secret plan to do something bad.
example: The detective uncovered the plot to steal the diamonds.
note: Italian 'trama' means the storyline of a book or film, which is a different meaning. Changed to 'complotto' so all four match the definition.

definition: A single idea or opinion in a discussion.
example: She made an important point during the meeting.
note: Same word appears twice in the list; corrected the same way so the two entries agree. Had been pushed onto 'the sharp tip of a pen', which is a rare use.

definition: Perhaps; it may be true.
example: She might possibly arrive late for the meeting today.
note: Italian 'possibilmente' is a false friend: it means 'if possible', not 'perhaps'. Changed to 'forse'.

definition: To act as if something is true when it is not.
example: The children pretend to be superheroes playing in the park.
note: French 'prétendre' is a false friend: it means 'to claim', not 'to pretend'. Changed to 'faire semblant'.

definition: An official proof of training or skill.
example: She earned a qualification in web development from the local college.
note: Italian 'qualificazione' is the word used for getting through to the next round in sport. The word for a certificate or skill is 'qualifica'.

definition: To make a product available to the public.
example: The company will release a new product next month.
note: Italian 'rilasciare' is mostly used for issuing documents. 'Lanciare' matches the Spanish and French and fits launching a product.

definition: Far away from other places; hard to reach.
example: They live in a remote village in the mountains.
note: The example did not even use the headword; it used 'remotely'. Rewritten. French 'à distance' meant 'from a distance', which is a different idea; changed so all four mean 'far away'.

definition: To move upward, especially the sun coming up in the morning.
example: The sun will rise in the east every morning.
note: Same word appears twice in the list; corrected the same way so the two entries agree.

definition: Having an uneven surface; not smooth.
example: The cat has a rough tongue.
note: Spanish was missing its accent. German 'rauh' is the old spelling; the modern spelling is 'rau'.

definition: To fire a gun or other weapon.
example: The soldier was told not to shoot without an order.
note: Had been pushed onto the rare meaning of a plant growing upward, and the Spanish was left as 'it will grow', a conjugated form rather than a word a learner can use. The first meaning of 'shoot' is to fire a weapon, which is what the original French showed. Rebuilt around that.

definition: The use of money to buy things.
example: Her spending on books has gone up this year.
note: The headword and definition describe a thing, but all four translations had been turned into the action. Restored to the thing, and the example now shows it as a thing.

definition: A long thin piece of wood.
example: The dog carried a stick in its mouth.
note: Every one of the four original translations was the piece of wood, and all four had been changed to the action of gluing things. A stick is the first thing a learner pictures. Fully restored.

definition: A long thin piece of wood.
example: The dog carried a stick in its mouth.
note: Same word appears twice in the list; corrected the same way so the two entries agree.

definition: Thin cord used for tying things.
example: She tied the parcel with a piece of string.
note: The entry taught only the narrow computer meaning. The original French was 'ficelle', the everyday cord, which is the first meaning of 'string'. Rebuilt around that.

definition: To turn a device off.
example: Please switch off the lights when you leave.
note: Three of the four translations meant 'to turn off' but German 'schalten' was neutral, so it did not match. Changed to 'ausschalten', and the definition now matches the example.
